name: Kinetic type
basis: animated type rows masking the picture (how)

lumenary.blurb: Giant sliding type with your picture showing through the letters.

facts.bestOn: Colourful, busy pictures that fill the frame

why: Type is usually something you read, but set huge and moving it becomes a window. This treatment fills the screen with heavy words that slide in alternating directions, and lets the picture show only through the letters. Because every row travels at its own speed and starts at its own phase, the composition never repeats exactly.
how: Set the words in an extra heavy typeface and repeat them along each row with a gap.
Slide every row at its own speed, alternating direction, with each row starting at a different phase.
Draw all filled rows in white on a separate mask.
Brighten the picture with a gamma curve and keep it only where the mask is opaque.
Draw the outline rows as strokes on top of the background.
history: Moving type became a craft in the 1950s and 60s through title designers such as Saul Bass, whose opening for North by Northwest in 1959 is often cited as an early landmark. Desktop animation software in the 1990s opened it to everyone, and lyric videos, sports promos and social media captions now rely on it constantly.
terms: Text that moves as part of the design.
A shape that decides which parts of an image stay visible.
A curve that brightens or darkens mid tones without changing black and white.
paragraphs: The words are rendered in an extra-heavy typeface, repeated along each row with a gap between repeats, and every row slides at its own speed in alternating directions. The speed of row i is a base speed times a factor that cycles through three values, and each row starts at a different phase, so the rows never line up and the composition keeps changing.

The picture appears through the letters by masking. All filled rows are drawn in white into a separate mask canvas; the picture (brightened first) is drawn into a third canvas, and the “destination-in” blend keeps the picture only where the mask is opaque. Nothing is cut out pixel by pixel: the compositor does a per-pixel multiplication of picture by mask for us. Outline rows are drawn directly as strokes on top of the background. The brighten slider is a gamma curve applied through a 256-entry lookup table, so the cost is one table read per channel.

equations.note: Horizontal position of row i: direction d_i = ±1 alternates, w is the width of one repeat of the words.
Destination-in compositing: picture colour times the mask’s alpha.
Gamma lift; g < 1 brightens the mid-tones.

presets.text: Fewer, bigger rows let the picture read through clearly.
Many rows at high speed feel like a ticker wall.
